audit.whatIsWrong: whys[6] reads 'With two-plus items his MR, taunt and shield flip it to Galio' while win[6] reads Darius, and the late paragraph says the same thing at length. One row contradicts its own verdict.
audit.why: Darius wins this 52.39% over 3098 games and galio's table carries 47.61%, so the two sum to 100.0. galio's disk chart is Skill, Darius, Darius, Skill, Skill, Darius, Darius with ratings 5/5/5/4/4/5/5 - identical sides to this page and properly inverse ratings, so the chart is mirror-locked and correct. The two claims reconcile once the stage is read as the side lane: Galio's two-item value is peel and a global ultimate, neither of which helps him in a 1v1 against a champion who can pull him.
audit.corrected: He scales as a peel tank, but the side-lane 1v1 stays yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why is the generic Noxian Guillotine line and never mentions Hero's Entrance, which is the only thing that changes at 6 in this lane. phases[0].why says 'Your AA + W chop wins most level-1 exchanges' under a phase whose side is Skill.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140 seconds at 4000/4750/5500 range and 'designates an ally's position as his landing spot, granting all allies in the area a magic shield' before the knock-up. It is not a duelling spike, which the page correctly says elsewhere - but the shield on arrival is what turns a won 1v1 into a lost 2v1, and that is worth stating at the stage it appears. At level 1, Colossal Smash gives him a periodic empowered basic attack that deals bonus magic damage in an area, which is exactly the kind of free answer that makes a level-1 chop war even rather than yours.
audit.corrected: Noxian Guillotine turns any 5-stack trade into a kill, but Hero's Entrance is 180s of global shield - his ally arrives with him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield of Durand is referred to six times as 'his W shield' or 'his W taunt' and its actual mechanic is never stated anywhere on the page - not the charge-up, not the 275-unit radius, not the 18-second cooldown. Justice Punch is named as the tracked cooldown in twelve fields and described only as 'His dash + knockup engage', with no number and no tell. Winds of War is called a tornado without the detail that makes it dodgeable.
audit.why: Shield of Durand (W, 18/17/16/15/14s, 275 range): 'Galio charges a defensive stance, moving slowly. Upon releasing the charge, Galio will taunt and damage nearby enemies.' Three things follow that the page never says: the taunt is not instant, he is slowed while he holds it, and its radius is 275 units - so a step backward during the wind-up beats the ability outright. That is the single most actionable fact in the matchup and 18 seconds is a long punish window. Justice Punch (E, 11/10/9/8/7s, 650 range): 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters' - the backstep is the visual tell, and it means a Galio standing next to you moves away from you before he commits. Winds of War (Q, 11/10/9/8/7s, 825 range) 'fires two windblasts that converge into a large tornado' - the damage is at the convergence, so the player is walking out of one point rather than a whole area.
audit.corrected: Shield of Durand is an 18s charge that only taunts on release, inside 275 units - step out during the wind-up. Justice Punch is 11s and he steps backward before he charges.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Justice Punch with no number, then fills the remaining two bullets with placeholders ('Your engage/committal tool', 'Your ultimate') that carry no information.
audit.why: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7, Shield of Durand 18/17/16/15/14, Winds of War 11/10/9/8/7, Hero's Entrance 180/160/140, against Apprehend at 26/23.5/21/18.5/16. Shield of Durand's 18 seconds is the longest of Galio's basic cooldowns and the one worth planning a commit around.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch 11s at 650 range with a backstep tell; Shield of Durand 18s, charged, 275 units; Hero's Entrance 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Galio's opener is an empowered auto-attack rather than an ability cast.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/_missing/darius.json flags this matchup with the autoreset-burst-tell rule for Colossal Smash. Riot's text: 'Every few seconds, Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area.' Against a champion who is deciding whether to step into a chop war at level 1, knowing his damage arrives on an auto rather than a spell is what makes the decision.
audit.corrected: Colossal Smash gives him a periodic empowered auto that answers your chop.

edits.after: Galio scales into a peel tank: Shield of Durand is an 18s charge that taunts on release inside 275 units, and Hero's Entrance is 180s of shielding for every ally at the landing spot. Duel him early; late, fight where he is not.

edits.before: Two-plus items is where Galio earns his keep. Stacked magic resist and his W shield blunt your burst, his taunt cancels your all-in, and Hero's Entrance lets him decide teamfights map-wide. He beats you as a scaling utility tank, so cash your early lead and don't try to solo him in the late game.
edits.after: Two-plus items is where Galio earns his keep, but not against you one-on-one. Shield of Durand is 18s and has to charge before it taunts, so a 275-unit step ruins it. His real value is Hero's Entrance at 180s deciding fights map-wide, so cash your early lead and fight where he is not.

notes: Galio's kit file flags Justice Punch with 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Riot's description is 'Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters' - there is no terrain creation anywhere in it, so I treated the flag as a tooltip-parse misfire and never wrote it. Nothing on this page asserts what a taunt does to Darius specifically: the existing copy says Shield of Durand 'locks your Apprehend all-in down', and whether a taunt blocks ability casts outright is game-mechanics detail that is not in either kit file, so I described the ability's shape (charged, 275 units, taunts on release) and left the consequence as the page already had it. Also unverified and left alone: whether Justice Punch's knock-up interrupts Noxian Guillotine's leap. diff reads FAV while report[14].t and breakdown.difficulty say 'Even matchup - difficulty 6/10'; at a 52.39% win rate both readings are arguable, so I left the label alone rather than guess.
